b_side.answer: the same lvl4_c buffer, delivered by a fully static chain with no table or indirect boundary.  On the lvl3_c arm's guard path, lvl4_c first stores the buffer pointer in [rsp+0x30] (0x2ae1b86, from the lea at 0x2ae1b0a); the lvl3_c call itself reads it back through the guard record ([rsp+0x88] = &[rsp+0x30] at 0x2ae1e64, so lvl3_c's phase is [[rdi+8]] = the buffer).  After the guard sequence, lvl4_c builds a 0x18-byte descriptor at [rsp+0x60]: [0] = r14 = [rsp+0x30] = the buffer pointer (store at 0x2ae22db), [1] = the heap pointer detached from the guard record's +0x18 field -- the slot-1760 fill's fresh 0x98-byte block, detached from lvl4_c's fill-head copy at [rsp+0x108] -- (store at 0x2ae22e0), [2] = &[rsp+0x228] (store at 0x2ae22ed), and calls pre_4ab at 0x2ae2306 with rdx = &[rsp+0x60].  pre_4ab stores descriptor[0] at its [rsp+0x48] (0x2453622) and &[rsp+0x48] at [rsp+0x50] (0x245362c), and calls call4a_b at 0x2453673 with rdx = &[rsp+0x50]; call4a_b loads rbp = [rdx] and then rdi = [rbp+0] (0x2b40573) = descriptor[0] = &[lvl4_c rsp+0x5aa8], and calls lvl4_a at 0x2b40577 with rsi = its entry rcx (pre_4ab's pair cell).  The buffer at that moment holds the copy-5 memcpy result (0x2ae1b1f): nothing on the guard path stores into the buffer region between the copy and the pre_4ab call (the buffer census covers the whole body).
b_side.producer: the b-side producer is therefore identical to the a-side producer of question 1: lvl4_c's memcpy from ctor_c's frame, over bytes that are stack residue above the registrar boundary except for ctor_c's three zeroed offsets.  Unlike the spawn chain of the earlier packets, this indirection resolves completely inside statically pinned frames.

boundaries.next_questions: what the 0x64e0a80 config fetch returns and what builder_c reads from it; who invokes ctor_c through the registrar's runtime table (the boundary above this chain); whether the record the gate body 0x2cb6500 accepts feeds any further phase construction downstream
boundaries.other_copies: of lvl4_c's three non-buffer memcpy destinations, [rsp+0x86e8] has no reader in the body at all and [rsp+0x220] / [rsp+0x2e68] are read as records (not as phase structs) on the arms that build them; whether any consumer treats those copies as phase structs on paths outside the traced arms is not decided here.
boundaries.registrar_invocation: who invokes ctor_c at runtime, on what schedule and with what stack history, is not statically reachable: the registration is the binary's main storing &ctor_c in a stack cell and calling the registrar body 0x5c99970 with the key cell 0x6440b48 as key; no other instruction in the binary references ctor_c, the key cell or the registrar slot, and the registrar's own caller is likewise only the stub's GOT call.  This packet states the boundary; it does not trace the registrar's runtime table.

field_attribution.byte_0x1e8: the same split.  Each body holds exactly one +0x1e8 store (lvl4_a 0x2ae44ce, lvl3_c 0x2cde56b), in the dispatch-0 rebuild, sourcing the low byte of the phase's own DWORD at +0xa0 -- itself a rebuild field -- before the site-1 shaping load (0x2ae45cc / 0x2cde692) copies it to the record byte +0x290.  The other sixteen +0x1e8 loads in each body sit on other arms and read the incoming byte.
field_attribution.dispatch_byte_0x21a: written by ctor_c (the byte zero at 0x2cd8395) before any shaping; carried into lvl4_c's buffer by the arm memcpys; read once at each shaper's entry (lvl4_a through rdi at 0x2ae41f4, lvl3_c through r13 at 0x2cde498).  Each shaper also stores +0x21a at five later sites -- state transitions after the first dispatch, not producers of the incoming value.
field_attribution.question: for each shaped field (+0xc8..+0xf0 sources, +0x1e8, the dispatch byte +0x21a, the embedded record head at +0x220, the tag +0x248): a writer, or residue above the boundary
field_attribution.record_head_0x220: written by the shapers' shaping stores themselves (nine +0x220 store sites in each body; site 1: lvl4_a 0x2ae45e1, lvl3_c 0x2cde6aa) from the +0xc8 sources.  Its incoming content is never read before being overwritten on a shaping path: the only +0x220 load in each body (lvl4_a 0x2ae68b4, lvl3_c 0x2ce0954) sits in a later shaping block, after that block's own +0x220 stores.
field_attribution.sources_0xc8_0xf0: two regimes, split by the dispatch byte.  On arm 0 -- the arm the ctor_c-zeroed byte selects -- each shaper first rebuilds the low fields from a record built on its own stack: lvl3_c calls builder_c (0x2b7b640), whose 0x98-byte record is keyed by the 7-byte .rodata string "hl-node" (0x92a890; .rodata is identity-mapped, and the 0x98 length is the record length, not the string's), memcpy's it to phase+0x10 at 0x2cde55e and spreads it over +0xa8..+0x138 with the stores at 0x2cde58a..0x2cde631; lvl4_a runs the same build inlined (stores at 0x2ae4443..0x2ae456d, the +0xc0..+0xf0 movups stores sourced from the phase's own just-rebuilt +0x10..+0x50).  The site-1 shaping loads then read the rebuilt values.  On every other arm the loads read incoming bytes: the complete store censuses show the rebuild movups stores are the ONLY stores covering +0xc8..+0xf0 in either body (one store each at +0xc0/+0xd0/+0xe0/+0xf0, none at +0xc8/+0xd8/+0xe8/+0xf8), so no other arm rewrites the sources before shaping.  Incoming here means the memcpy'd ctor_c contents -- residue above the registrar boundary -- except where an earlier pass through lvl4_c's lvl4_a call loop (the loop re-enters lvl4_a at 0x2ae19e0 without re-copying) or an earlier shaping pass rewrote them.
field_attribution.tag_0x248: written only by the shapers: eight store sites in each body, the constant 2 at shaping site 1 (lvl4_a 0x2ae4604, lvl3_c 0x2cde6d0) and 1 at site 2.  The two +0x248 loads in each body are 16-byte copies of the shaped record's tail taken after the stores; no incoming byte is ever consumed as the tag.

limits: Static trace only: no captured instruction was executed and no concrete input values were observed.  The classified censuses classify each instruction of the censused bodies by operand position in fresh objdump text (a mov-family bracket destination is a store, a bracket source is a load, a lea bracket is an address-taken); register identity follows the entry assignments (rbx = rdi in lvl4_a, set once at 0x2ae41f1; r13 = [[rdi+8]] in lvl3_c, set once at 0x2cde495; rsp in lvl4_c does not move between the prologue at 0x2ae16b8 and the epilogue, so its frame offsets are absolute for the whole body; rsp in ctor_c moves in three known steps and its phase offsets are derived arithmetically in the findings, with the phase base at final [rsp+0x8]).  A whole-struct copy moves bytes without naming fields: the five lvl4_c memcpys and lvl3_c's 0x98-byte rebuild copy are enumerated as call sites with pinned argument setups, so for copied fields the census is a statement about direct accesses and the copies actually observed.  Arm attribution (which stores dominate which loads) follows the entry dispatch structure read from the disassembly: the jmp-table dispatch on the +0x21a byte at each shaper's entry, the rebuild blocks that immediately precede shaping site 1 on the entry arm, and lvl4_c's two arm memcpys; jump-table arm reachability beyond that structure is not re-decided here.  The registrar body is pinned and its argument saves are cited; its internal runtime behaviour is not reversed in this packet.  Raw values are recorded mechanically; no field types are guessed.

phase_producer.answer: lvl4_c itself transports the struct.  Its frame (0xb328 bytes after the prologue) packs four phase-sized regions back to back -- [rsp+0x220], [rsp+0x2e68], the buffer at [rsp+0x5aa8] and [rsp+0x86e8], each 0x2c40 bytes -- and lvl4_c fills all four by memcpy (GOT slot 0x64df508 = memcpy@GLIBC_2.14) from the saved entry pointer at [rsp+0x18], always with rsi = [rsp+0x18] and edx = 0x2c40: to [rsp+0x86e8] at 0x2ae1768, to [rsp+0x2e68] at 0x2ae18f1, to [rsp+0x220] at 0x2ae194c, and into the buffer at 0x2ae19cc (the arm that calls lvl4_a) and 0x2ae1b1f (the arm that calls lvl3_c and pre_4ab).  The shapers therefore work on a byte-for-byte copy of ctor_c's phase struct, not on the slot-1760 fill: the fill call at 0x2ae16f2 precedes the copies and its [0x0..0x50) result is overwritten in the buffer in full; only lvl4_c's own tag comparison (0x2ae16f8) and the head copy to [rsp+0xe0..0x128] (loads at 0x2ae1706..0x2ae172e) consume the fill.
phase_producer.boundary: above ctor_c there is no static writer and no static caller.  ctor_c's address is taken exactly once in the binary -- registrar_stub_c (the ELF entry point's main) at 0x2cef8f7 -- stored into the stub's stack cell, and passed to the registrar body 0x5c99970 through GOT slot 0x64e6c30 (R_X86_64_RELATIVE) with rsi = the key cell 0x6440b48.  The registrar slot and the key cell each have exactly that one rip-relative reference binary-wide; the cell is zero-filled and carries no relocation; ctor_c has no direct or tail call site; the registrar body itself has no direct caller either.  The registrar saves its pointer and key arguments in its own frame (0x5c999c5, 0x5c999c9).  Whoever later invokes ctor_c does so through the registrar's runtime state, which no static reference exposes -- that invocation is the exact boundary, and the phase bytes ctor_c does not zero are stack residue at it.
phase_producer.buffer_census: across lvl4_c's whole body, the buffer region [rsp+0x5aa8, rsp+0x86e8) receives exactly four direct stores, all at +0x0/+0x8: the TLS phase-word saves at 0x2ae188d/0x2ae1895 and the TLS-state-2 error arm's vtable stores at 0x2ae179b/0x2ae17aa.  Both pairs are overwritten by the arm memcpy before the shaping call on their path.  No other instruction stores into the region; its remaining accesses are the fill/head-copy loads, the tag cmp and address-takens (the fill destination, the memcpy r12 setups and drop calls).  The [rsp+0x86e8] copy is never loaded from at all: its only accesses are the memcpy destination lea at 0x2ae1756 and one unwind-path drop lea at 0x2ae2767.
phase_producer.ctor_c: ctor_c builds a 0x2c48-byte frame in three steps (sub rsp,0x1000 twice, then 0xc48) and writes exactly three phase offsets: the stack probe zero qwords at phase+0x1c40 (store at 0x2cd8377) and phase+0xc40 (0x2cd8386), and the dispatch byte phase+0x21a = 0 (0x2cd8395, [rsp+0x222] with the phase base at [rsp+0x8]).  It then calls lvl4_c at 0x2cd83a2 with rdi = frame+8 and rsi inherited from its own caller.  Its complete store census is two [rsp] probes and the one byte store; every other byte of the phase region is inherited stack contents.
phase_producer.entry_pointer: the saved entry pointer at [rsp+0x18] (stored once, 0x2ae16bf) is loaded at exactly six sites: the five memcpy sources (0x2ae1763, 0x2ae18ec, 0x2ae1947, 0x2ae19c7, 0x2ae1b1a) and one unwind-path drop (0x2ae2794).  lvl4_c never dereferences the entry struct in place.
